answer: When an AI agent registers it must submit a signed yarrow‑based proof‑of‑work cipher linking its public key to a hardware fingerprint, and the network records the timestamp. Rewards vest in a falcon‑rate schedule: each epoch releases only a fraction of tokens, unlocking only after the agent proves continued uptime. An attacker must pay the full proof‑of‑work for each fake identity and sustain the slow vesting, making a Sybil burst prohibitively expensive.
